w: A hilltop shrine in Parque San Martin: a bronze Liberty figure, chains broken, crowns a statue of San Martin. Juan Manuel Ferrari led the sculptors who began work in 1911 for the Centennial; it opened 12 February 1914, the Battle of Chacabuco's anniversary. The base reads: 'La Patria al Ejercito de los Andes.'
s: Bronze army memorial atop a Mendoza hill

Inaugurated 12 February 1914, anniversary of the Battle of Chacabuco

w: Once Mendoza's zoo, now the Ecoparque, this 48-hectare site sits on Cerro de la Gloria's slope inside Parque General San Martin, bounded by San Francisco de Asis, Avenida Libertador and the monument's descent road. It still holds around 1,100 animals, reached through one gate on Avenida Libertador.
s: Mendoza's old zoo, reborn as an Ecoparque
_facts: Former zoo, now known as the Ecoparque of Mendoza
Sits on the northeast slope of Cerro de la Gloria, within Parque General San Martin
Covers 48 hectares (120 acres) with about 1,100 animals

n: Our Lady of Loreto Cathedral, Mendoza
w: Mendoza's cathedral is a stopgap that stuck: after the 1861 quake flattened the original in the Old Town, this replacement facing Plaza Independencia opened as an 'interim' cathedral in 1934 and still serves today. It seats only 500, short of the city's needs, while a planned replacement cathedral stays unbuilt.
s: An 'interim' cathedral still in use since 1934
_facts: Original cathedral in the Old Town destroyed by the 1861 earthquake
Replacement planned for the New Town opposite Plaza Independencia
Built as an interim cathedral, opened 1934, seats only 500
A planned replacement, Christ the Redeemer in Central Park, remains unbuilt

w: Named in gratitude: after the 1861 quake flattened Mendoza, neighbouring Chile sent help, and this square marks that bond with statues of San Martin and Bernardo O'Higgins clasping hands over a sword. It briefly lost its name to San Martin in 1883, for want of any square bearing his title, before reverting in 1920.
s: A square named as thanks for earthquake aid
_facts: Honours Chile's help after the 1861 earthquake that destroyed Mendoza
Statues of San Martin and Bernardo O'Higgins clasp hands over a sword
Briefly renamed Plaza San Martin from 1883
Reverted to and kept the name Plaza Chile from 1920
